Add Range-Based Cover Proportion and Category Columns (Ordered Factors)

add_cover_categories.Rd

Classifies benthic cover values from a specified numeric column into:

  • A human-readable proportion range column: cover_prop

  • An ordinal category column: cover_cat with levels A (highest) to D (lowest)

Usage

add_cover_categories(
  df,
  column = "median",
  breaks = c(10, 30, 50),
  prop_labels = c("0 - 10%", "10 - 30%", "30 - 50%", "50 - 100%"),
  cat_labels = c("D", "C", "B", "A")
)

Arguments

df

A data frame containing a numeric column to classify.

column

Character. The name of the column to classify.

breaks

Numeric vector of length 3 giving the lower bounds for the second, third and fourth ranges respectively.

prop_labels

Character vector of length 4 defining the labels for the ranges, ordered from lowest to highest.

cat_labels

Character vector of length 4 defining category codes for the ranges, ordered from lowest to highest.

Value

The input data frame with two additional ordered factor columns:

  • cover_prop: One of prop_labels, ordered descending for plotting convenience.

  • cover_cat: One of cat_labels, ordered descending (e.g., A > B > C > D).

Details

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df <- data.frame(median = c(NA, 5, 10, 15, 30, 35, 50, 55, 100))
add_cover_categories(df, column = "median")

# Custom breaks and labels
add_cover_categories(
  df, column = "median",
  breaks = c(10, 25, 40),
  prop_labels = c("0 - 10%", "10 - 25%", "25 - 40%", "40 - 100%"),
  cat_labels  = c("D", "C", "B", "A")
)
} # }
